introduction.situation: Chemistry studies substances, their kinds, their architecture, their energetics and their changes.
introduction.complication: The source groups mix library headings, classes of substances, phenomena and methods, so there is no single clear view of how the field is divided.
introduction.question: How is everything in chemistry divided when seen as questions asked of a substance?
introduction.answer: Chemistry's objects divide by the question asked of a substance into its composition and identity, its structure and bonding, its equilibrium and energy, its rates and mechanisms, and its synthesis and analysis.

governing_thought: Chemistry's objects divide by the question asked of a substance into its composition and identity, its structure and bonding, its equilibrium and energy, its rates and mechanisms, and its synthesis and analysis.

key_line.mece_dimension: the question asked of a substance
key_line.rank_note: The questions run from what a substance is, through how it is built and how it settles and changes, to how it is made or found.

points.statement: Composition and identity is the question of what a substance is, covering its general kind, role and chemical or biological class.
points.name: Composition and identity is the question of what a substance is, covering its general kind, role and chemical or biological class.

support.rank_note: From the most general entities to the more specialised classes of substance.

points.statement: General entities and roles name the broad kinds of chemical object and the functions they play.
points.name: General entities and roles name the broad kinds of chemical object and the functions they play.

support.rank_note: From entities to the roles they play.

points.statement: Chemical entities name the broad kinds of object, from atoms to molecular entities and groups.
points.name: Chemical entities name the broad kinds of object, from atoms to molecular entities and groups.

support.rank_note: From the most general entity to the smallest.

points.statement: Roles name the function a substance plays, from the general notion to its biological and chemical forms.
points.name: Roles name the function a substance plays, from the general notion to its biological and chemical forms.

support.rank_note: From the general role to its specialisations.

points.name: General and element-family inorganic classes identify substances by the kinds of elements they contain.

points.name: Metal-centred classes identify substances by transition, f-block and organometallic metal centres.

points.statement: Organic and ring-based classes identify substances by their carbon frameworks.
points.name: Organic and ring-based classes identify substances by their carbon frameworks.

points.statement: Biological classes identify substances by their biochemical nature as macromolecules, enzymes, hormones and nutrients.
points.name: Biological classes identify substances by their biochemical nature as macromolecules, enzymes, hormones and nutrients.

points.name: Medicinal and biomolecular classes identify substances by their biological activity and their use in medicine.

points.name: Medicinal and biomolecular fields ask what a substance does in living systems and how it is modelled.

points.name: Biologically active substances and their effects identify substances by what they do in living systems.

points.name: Chemicals and drugs and their medical materials identify substances by the practical use made of them.

points.name: Condensed and extended structures ask how atoms and molecules are assembled into solids, frameworks and materials.

points.name: Crystalline and framework solids ask how atoms are ordered in extended solid structures.

support.rank_note: From crystals to frameworks.

points.statement: Macromolecular and nanoscale materials ask how larger assemblies are organised and how their internal motion behaves.
points.name: Macromolecular and nanoscale materials ask how larger assemblies are organised and how their internal motion behaves.

points.name: Fields that ask what a material or molecular assembly is made of and how its structure and internal motion are organised.

points.statement: Macromolecular and materials chemistry not elsewhere classified
points.name: Macromolecular and materials chemistry not elsewhere classified

points.name: Intermolecular interactions and structure concern how molecules attract one another, are arranged, and are probed.

points.name: Molecular imaging (incl. electron microscopy and neutron diffraction)

points.statement: Measured properties and their theory ask what quantities and responses a substance displays and how they are computed.
points.name: Measured properties and their theory ask what quantities and responses a substance displays and how they are computed.

support.rank_note: From measured quantities to theoretical design.

points.statement: Measured properties are quantities that can be determined on a substance or solution.
points.name: Measured properties are quantities that can be determined on a substance or solution.

points.statement: Solubility, specific gravity, and viscosity are kinds of physical property, each defined by a different question asked of a substance.
points.name: Solubility, specific gravity, and viscosity are kinds of physical property, each defined by a different question asked of a substance.

points.statement: Fields that ask how a substance interacts with light and what measurable properties it displays.
points.name: Fields that ask how a substance interacts with light and what measurable properties it displays.

points.name: Fields that ask how a material can be conceived and designed in theory to achieve desired properties, and how it behaves in aggregate.

points.title: Structure and bonding

points.statement: Equilibrium and energy is the question of how a substance settles into states, exchanges matter and energy and moves between phases.
points.name: Equilibrium and energy is the question of how a substance settles into states, exchanges matter and energy and moves between phases.

support.rank_note: From energetics to states and phases to transfer across boundaries.

points.statement: Energetics and solution states ask how energy, charge and solvent govern a substance at equilibrium.
points.name: Energetics and solution states ask how energy, charge and solvent govern a substance at equilibrium.

support.rank_note: From thermodynamics to solutions to stored energy.

points.statement: Energy and structure probes ask how a substance stores energy, ignites, presents its surface, or reveals its atomic arrangement.
points.name: Energy and structure probes ask how a substance stores energy, ignites, presents its surface, or reveals its atomic arrangement.

support.rank_note: Ranked from the most direct structural measurement (X-ray diffraction) to surface behavior to energetic phenomena.

points.statement: Phase and state changes ask how a substance separates, converts or deteriorates into another condition.
points.name: Phase and state changes ask how a substance separates, converts or deteriorates into another condition.

support.rank_note: From solid formation to other changes of state to degradation.

points.statement: Solid-forming processes are those in which a solid phase emerges or separates out of a solution or melt.
points.name: Solid-forming processes are those in which a solid phase emerges or separates out of a solution or melt.

support.rank_note: Ordered by structure: ordered solid growth first, then general solid separation.

points.statement: Changes of state or form describe a substance converting into a different physical or chemical condition.
points.name: Changes of state or form describe a substance converting into a different physical or chemical condition.

support.rank_note: Listed in structural order of change type.

points.statement: Material behavior concepts describe how a substance's properties vary with direction or how it deteriorates through reaction with its environment.
points.name: Material behavior concepts describe how a substance's properties vary with direction or how it deteriorates through reaction with its environment.

support.rank_note: Ordered by structure: an intrinsic property first, then a degradation process.

points.statement: Interfaces, barriers and gradients ask how a substance crosses, exchanges across or is held at a boundary.
points.name: Interfaces, barriers and gradients ask how a substance crosses, exchanges across or is held at a boundary.

support.rank_note: From surfaces to barriers to gradient-driven and general movement.

points.statement: Questions about interfaces and uptake ask how a substance interacts with surfaces, other phases and ions, taking material in or holding it at a boundary.
points.name: Questions about interfaces and uptake ask how a substance interacts with surfaces, other phases and ions, taking material in or holding it at a boundary.

support.rank_note: Kinds of interface questions arranged by structure: surface science, bulk uptake, surface binding, and ionization of air.

points.statement: Gradient-driven processes ask how a substance moves or exchanges in response to concentration or charge differences.
points.name: Gradient-driven processes ask how a substance moves or exchanges in response to concentration or charge differences.

support.rank_note: Ordered by structure; no ranking implied.

points.statement: Movement and release phenomena describe how matter or energy gets through or out of a substance.
points.name: Movement and release phenomena describe how matter or energy gets through or out of a substance.

support.rank_note: Listed in structural order of movement type.

points.title: Equilibrium and energy

points.statement: Rates and mechanisms is the question of how fast a substance changes and by what steps its bonds are rearranged.
points.name: Rates and mechanisms is the question of how fast a substance changes and by what steps its bonds are rearranged.

support.rank_note: From general kinetics and catalysis to specific kinds of reaction.

points.statement: Kinetics and catalysis ask how fast and by what route a reaction proceeds.
points.name: Kinetics and catalysis ask how fast and by what route a reaction proceeds.

support.rank_note: From kinetics to catalysis.

points.statement: Specific reaction types ask how particular driving conditions or bond changes transform a substance.
points.name: Specific reaction types ask how particular driving conditions or bond changes transform a substance.

support.rank_note: From light and heat driven to bond-rearranging reactions.

points.statement: Light, heat and water driven reactions transform a substance by an external driving condition.
points.name: Light, heat and water driven reactions transform a substance by an external driving condition.

support.rank_note: From light to heat to water.

points.statement: Bond-rearranging reactions transform a substance by changing its own bonds or molecular structure.
points.name: Bond-rearranging reactions transform a substance by changing its own bonds or molecular structure.

support.rank_note: From general transformation to polymerisation.

points.statement: Transformation phenomena are changes in which a substance's own bonds or molecular structure are rearranged, as in organic chemistry, redox, and polymerization.
points.name: Transformation phenomena are changes in which a substance's own bonds or molecular structure are rearranged, as in organic chemistry, redox, and polymerization.

support.rank_note: Ordered by the kind of structural change to the substance.

points.title: Rates and mechanisms

points.statement: Synthesis and analysis is the question of how a substance is made, isolated, detected and measured.
points.name: Synthesis and analysis is the question of how a substance is made, isolated, detected and measured.

support.rank_note: From making substances to finding and measuring them.

points.statement: Synthetic and organic approaches ask how substances are built and what they are used for.
points.name: Synthetic and organic approaches ask how substances are built and what they are used for.

support.rank_note: From biological substances to organic reactions to identity and use.

points.statement: Each concept is a kind of question asked of a biological substance, from the general characterisation of macromolecules to the specific study of sugar-bearing conjugates.

points.name: Identity-focused and framing concepts ask what an organic substance is and what it is used for, covering the whole field, natural bioactive compounds, uncategorised topics and applications.

points.statement: Analytical methods ask how a substance is identified and quantified by instruments and spectra.
points.name: Analytical methods ask how a substance is identified and quantified by instruments and spectra.

support.rank_note: From the general field to specific instrumental methods.

points.statement: Instrumental methods (excl. immunological and bioassay methods)
points.name: Instrumental methods (excl. immunological and bioassay methods)

points.statement: Separation and sensing ask how components are isolated and detected in mixtures and forensic or residual cases.
points.name: Separation and sensing ask how components are isolated and detected in mixtures and forensic or residual cases.

support.rank_note: Isolation precedes detection.

points.statement: Separation, flow and sensing approaches answer what a substance is mixed with and where it is, by isolating components or detecting them continuously.

points.statement: Quality assurance, chemometrics, traceability and metrological chemistry
points.name: Quality assurance, chemometrics, traceability and metrological chemistry

support.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from separating components to moving samples to detecting them.
